request: Before any capital buffers or other add-ons, what minimum common equity tier 1, tier 1, total capital and leverage ratios must a Board-regulated institution maintain under the text of 12 CFR Part 217 reproduced on the cited page?
On days when direct-transmission filings are accepted, what is the daily submission window in the text of 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) reproduced on the cited page, and which days are excluded?

In the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 adopted on 15 May 2014, by when must an investment firm report complete and accurate details of transactions it has executed to the competent authority?
For 2025, according to IRS Publication 550, what is the Net Investment Income Tax rate, and to which amount is that rate applied?
In the original text of Directive 2009/138/EC, what probability and time horizon are used to describe the Solvency Capital Requirement, and what equivalent ruin frequency is stated?

An FDIC-supervised institution holds $80 million fair value of level 2A liquid assets and $30 million fair value of level 2B liquid assets as of the calculation date, and all are eligible HQLA. Ignoring other caps and adjustments, what level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts result under the text of 12 CFR Part 329 reproduced on the cited page, and what is their sum?

A covered company subject to the single-counterparty credit limits in 12 CFR Part 252 has $40 billion of tier 1 capital and an $11 billion aggregate net credit exposure to one counterparty. As in force on 2026-11-21, what is its 25% exposure cap in dollars, by how much does the exposure exceed that cap, and is the separate 5% economic-interdependence and control-relationship assessment triggered?

A registrant's named executive officer has perquisites and personal benefits totalling $120,000, including items worth $24,000 and $26,000. Under 17 CFR 229.402(c) as in force on 2026-11-21, may the registrant exclude perquisites altogether, what is the footnote quantification threshold, and which of those two items must be quantified?

An advanced approaches national bank that is not a savings and loan holding company has a legacy checklist using the OCC transition standards for calendar year 2014. What minimum common equity tier 1 and tier 1 capital ratios applied from January 1 through December 31, 2014, and what are the corresponding minimum ratios in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page? Ignore buffers and other add-ons.

According to HMRC's rates and allowances guidance, for non-ring fence profits under the rules from 1 April 2023, is there still a single Corporation Tax rate? State the rate for profits of £50,000 or less, the main rate for profits above £250,000, and the treatment of profits between those amounts.
A Federal branch of a foreign bank asks which minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio 12 CFR Part 3 imposes directly on that branch. What is the answer as in force on 2026-11-21?

An institution is scoping the annual privacy notice obligation in 17 CFR Part 248, subpart A. Apart from § 248.30(b), does that subpart cover information about companies or information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business purposes, as in force on 2026-11-21?

An EU payment institution provides only the payment service listed in point (6) of Annex I to the EU payment-services directive adopted in 2015. Under that directive's original text, what minimum capital must it maintain at all times?

Under the original text of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, by when must details of a derivative contract's conclusion, modification or termination be reported, and how long must counterparties keep records of a contract and its modifications?

(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. verdict.summary:
Scope and source

Source page: eCFR, 12 CFR Part 217, Subpart B, § 217.10, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-217/section-217.10 (fetched 2026-11-23T11:52:58Z, sha256 11713cd13188). Corroborated by the eCFR Subpart B page and the govinfo 2026 CFR text of Part 217. The operative provision is 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1).

Period: the regulatory minimums in the cited current text as of 2026-11-23. These are ongoing regulatory floors, not fiscal-period financial data. Currency: the ratios are dimensionless percentages; the underlying capital and exposure amounts are in USD as reported by the institution. Basis: risk-weighted assets for the CET1, Tier 1 and Total capital ratios; average total consolidated assets for the leverage ratio; total leverage exposure for the supplementary leverage ratio.

Answer before buffers or add-ons

| Ratio | Minimum | Source | Basis and arithmetic | Check |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Common equity tier 1 capital ratio | 4.5% | § 217.10(a)(1)(i) | CET1 capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(1). Arithmetic: 4.5% = 4.5 / 100 = 0.045. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Tier 1 capital ratio | 6% | § 217.10(a)(1)(ii) | Tier 1 capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(2). Arithmetic: 6% = 6 / 100 = 0.06. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Total capital ratio | 8% | § 217.10(a)(1)(iii) | Total capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(3). Arithmetic: 8% = 8 / 100 = 0.08. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Leverage ratio | 4% | § 217.10(a)(1)(iv) | Tier 1 capital divided by average total consolidated assets less deductions from tier 1 capital under § 217.22(a), (c) and (d), § 217.10(b)(4). Arithmetic: 4% = 4 / 100 = 0.04. | Separate from the risk-based ratios; not additive. |
| Supplementary leverage ratio, only for advanced approaches or Category III Board-regulated institutions | 3% | § 217.10(a)(1)(v) | Tier 1 capital divided by total leverage exposure, § 217.10(c)(1). Arithmetic: 3% = 3 / 100 = 0.03. | Additional institution-specific minimum; not a buffer and not applicable to all Board-regulated institutions. |

Provision text reproduced on the cited page

```text
§ 217.10 Minimum capital requirements.
(a) Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
(iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
(v) For advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.
```

Meaning of before buffers or add-ons

The table above reports only the § 217.10(a)(1) minima. It excludes any capital conservation buffer, stress capital buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, GSIB surcharge, or other buffer or add-on that would be layered on top of these floors elsewhere in Part 217. An institution subject to such an add-on must satisfy the minimum plus the applicable buffer or add-on; the amounts in this answer are the floors before that layering.

Institution-specific notes

1. Advanced approaches: after completing the parallel run process and receiving Board notification under § 217.121(d), an advanced approaches Board-regulated institution calculates its CET1, Tier 1 and Total capital ratios as the lower of the standardized calculation and the advanced approaches calculation under § 217.10(d)(1) through (3). The minimum percentage thresholds remain 4.5%, 6% and 8%.

2. Category III or advanced approaches: the supplementary leverage ratio minimum is 3% under § 217.10(a)(1)(v). The general leverage ratio minimum remains 4% under § 217.10(a)(1)(iv).

3. Qualifying community banking organization: under § 217.10(a)(2), a qualifying community banking organization subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in § 217.10(a). The CBLR framework has its own ratio, which is not reproduced on the cited page and is therefore not quantified here.

4. Historical transition: the 2014 phase-in values of 4.0% CET1 and 5.5% Tier 1 that appear in the transition provisions are historical and are not the current § 217.10(a)(1) minimums. They are not used in this answer.

Verification

All fetched copies of the cited text agree on the operative values: 4.5%, 6%, 8%, 4%, and the 3% supplementary leverage ratio for advanced approaches or Category III institutions. The hierarchy is internally consistent: 4.5% CET1 is below 6% Tier 1, which is below 8% Total capital. The leverage ratio and supplementary leverage ratio are separate, non-additive requirements. No currency conversion or rounding is involved because the figures are stated regulatory percentages.

Assumptions and limitations

This draft assumes the cited eCFR page is the operative text as of 2026-11-23 and that no later amendment changes § 217.10(a)(1). It assumes the institution is a Board-regulated institution that has not elected the community bank leverage ratio framework; if it has, § 217.10(a)(2) and the CBLR framework must be reviewed separately. This is a draft for review by a qualified finance, accounting or legal professional and is not regulatory, legal, tax or investment advice.

Editorial Note on Part 240




Editorial Note:


Nomenclature changes to part 240 appear at 57 FR 36501, Aug. 13, 1992, and 57 FR 47409, Oct. 16, 1992.






§ 240.0-2 Business hours of the Commission.




(a) The principal office of the Commission, at 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549, is open each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever currently is in effect in Washington, DC, provided that hours for the filing of documents pursuant to the Act or the rules and regulations thereunder are as set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.






(b) Submissions made in paper.  Paper documents filed with or otherwise furnished to the Commission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.






(c) Electronic filings.  Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.


Cross References:



For registration and exemption of exchanges, see §§ 240.6a-1 to 240.6a-3. For forms for permanent registration of securities, see § 240.12b-1. For regulations relating to registration of securities, see §§ 240.12b-1 to 240.12b-36. For forms for applications for registration of brokers and dealers, see §§ 240.15b1-1 to 240.15b9-1.


[58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023]

Editorial Note on Part 240




Editorial Note:


Nomenclature changes to part 240 appear at 57 FR 36501, Aug. 13, 1992, and 57 FR 47409, Oct. 16, 1992.






§ 240.0-2 Business hours of the Commission.




(a) The principal office of the Commission, at 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549, is open each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever currently is in effect in Washington, DC, provided that hours for the filing of documents pursuant to the Act or the rules and regulations thereunder are as set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.






(b) Submissions made in paper.  Paper documents filed with or otherwise furnished to the Commission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.






(c) Electronic filings.  Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.

verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE/COMPLIANCE PROFESSIONAL. Regulatory-text extraction, not legal, tax or investment advice. No currency amounts are involved; every number below is a clock time, and the basis (Washington, DC local time, EST or EDT whichever is in effect) is the basis the rule itself states.

=== 1. ANSWER IN ONE LINE ===
On days when direct-transmission (electronic) filings are accepted, 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) permits submission from 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect. The excluded days are Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays.

=== 2. VERBATIM TEXT OF § 240.0-2(c) AS REPRODUCED ON THE PAGES EXAMINED ===
"(c) Electronic filings. Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect."

Sources examined (both official; identical wording, character for character in the operative sentence):
- Source A — eCFR, 'current' title 17: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-240.0-2 ; also https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/part-240/section-240.0-2 and https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-240/subpart-A/subject-group-ECFRf2ef38fa463cdfa/section-240.0-2 . Fetched 2026-11-23T11:56:06Z; sha256 f86928af7bf9 (all three eCFR URLs returned the same hash, i.e. the same text).
- Source B — GovInfo, CFR 2025, Title 17, Volume 4: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol4/xhtml/CFR-2025-title17-vol4-sec240-0-2.html . Edition date 2025-04-01; fetched 2026-11-23T11:56:05Z; sha256 038795da7cb0.
- Corroborating — GovInfo chapter XML for the same volume (CFR-2025-title17-vol4-chapII.xml), fetched 2026-11-23T11:56:06Z, sha256 a13a122a73dd: reproduces paragraph (c) in the same words.

=== 3. SURROUNDING PARAGRAPHS, QUOTED FOR COMPLETENESS (context only — not the answer) ===
(a) "The principal office of the Commission, at 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549, is open each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever currently is in effect in Washington, DC, provided that hours for the filing of documents pursuant to the Act or the rules and regulations thereunder are as set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section."
(b) "Submissions made in paper. Paper documents filed with or otherwise furnished to the Commission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect."
Note the structure: paragraph (a) fixes office hours at 9:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m. but expressly displaces filing hours to (b) and (c); the paper window is 8:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; the direct-transmission (electronic) window is 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Do not use (a) or (b) as the answer to a direct-transmission question.

=== 4. AUTHORITY, EDITION AND AS-OF BASIS ===
Amendment history printed with the section on both sources: "[58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023]". The most recent amendment (2023) predates both the 2025 bound edition (edition date 2025-04-01) and the 2026-11-23 retrieval of the eCFR 'current' text, and the two agree verbatim. Conclusion: no edition conflict was observed between the current eCFR text and the 2025 bound CFR for this paragraph. As-of statement for the reviewer: text verified as of the retrieval timestamps above.

=== 5. EXTRACTED VALUES, WITH SOURCE AND ARITHMETIC ===
Value 1 — Daily submission window (ask 2).
  Window: 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
  Time basis: Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect in Washington, DC — i.e. the window is fixed in local clock time, so its UTC equivalent shifts by one hour at each DST transition. Any system control must be written on the local-clock definition, not on a fixed UTC offset.
  Duration arithmetic: 22:00 − 06:00 = 16 hours = 16 × 60 = 960 minutes.
  Period: daily, on days when direct-transmission filings are accepted.
  Currency: none (time values only).
Value 2 — Excluded days (ask 4).
  Saturdays; Sundays; Federal holidays.
  Count of categories: 3, exactly as enumerated in the text. The paragraph names no other closure category and contains no carry-forward, next-business-day or emergency-closure mechanic.
  Currency: none.

=== 6. COMPLIANCE COMMENTARY — SEPARATE FROM THE QUOTED TEXT ===
(a) Submission window is not the filing-date cutoff. § 240.0-2(c) states when the Commission will accept a direct transmission; it does not state when a filing is 'deemed filed' for deadline purposes. That convention sits in Regulation S-T (17 CFR Part 232) — generally, an electronic filing submitted after 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time is deemed filed the next business day. I have NOT reproduced that text verbatim here and it is not part of the quote in section 2; the reviewer should confirm the current wording of 17 CFR 232.13 before relying on it. Control implication if confirmed: the operative internal deadline for a same-day filing is 5:30 p.m. ET, and the 5:30 p.m.–10:00 p.m. remainder of the § 240.0-2(c) window is acceptance capacity, not deadline capacity. 5:30 p.m. falls inside the 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. window, so the two are consistent; no numeric conflict.
(b) 'Federal holidays' is not defined in § 240.0-2. Practical reference is the federal holiday schedule observed in Washington, DC. Ad hoc closures (weather, lapse in appropriations) are not addressed by the CFR text; check SEC/EDGAR published operating schedules and SEC closure announcements for the specific day. Flagged for the reviewer rather than asserted.
(c) Residual source limitation. The request refers to 'the cited page' but did not identify a URL or document. The answer above is taken verbatim from the two official reproductions in section 2, which agree. If the requester's cited page is a non-official reproduction (vendor manual, broker-dealer compliance guide, law-firm summary, exam module), compare that page line-by-line against Source A/B before reliance — a paraphrase there could state a different window or a shorter exclusion list.
(d) Scope of this memo. No financial-statement figures, thresholds, currency amounts, tax positions or investment conclusions are stated; nothing here is financial, tax or investment advice.

=== 7. REVIEWER CHECKLIST ===
1. Confirm the quoted sentence in section 2 against Source A or B at the URLs given.
2. Confirm the edition/as-of basis in section 4 is acceptable for the purpose at hand.
3. Confirm the deemed-filing cutoff in 17 CFR 232.13 (commentary (a)) before setting any internal deadline control at 5:30 p.m. ET.
4. Confirm the holiday calendar source and the treatment of ad hoc SEC closures (commentary (b)).
5. If the requester's 'cited page' is not Source A or B, obtain it and diff against the quote in section 2 (commentary (c)).

=== 8. LIMITATIONS ===
The specific page the requester had in mind was not identified; the answer is drawn from the official eCFR 'current' text and the GovInfo 2025 bound CFR, which are identical for this paragraph. No value in this memo was inferred, rounded or invented beyond the quoted text.

7.The reports shall be made to the competent authority either by the investment firm itself, an ARM acting on its behalf or by the trading venue through whose system the transaction was completed, in accordance with paragraphs 1, 3 and 9.
Investment firms shall have responsibility for the completeness, accuracy and timely submission of the reports which are submitted to the competent authority.

verdict.summary:
DRAFT NOTE FOR QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL REVIEW — NOT LEGAL, TAX OR INVESTMENT ADVICE

SUBJECT: Deadline for an investment firm to report complete and accurate details of executed transactions to the competent authority — original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 (MiFIR).

====================================================================
1. ANSWER (single sentence)
====================================================================
Under the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, an investment firm that executes transactions in financial instruments must report complete and accurate details of those transactions to the competent authority AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE, AND NO LATER THAN THE CLOSE OF THE FOLLOWING WORKING DAY.

Legal basis: Article 26(1), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014.

====================================================================
2. VERBATIM PROVISION (pinpoint citation)
====================================================================
Article 26 — 'Obligation to report transactions'
Paragraph 1, first subparagraph, in full:

  "Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments shall
   report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent
   authority as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the
   following working day."

Source of quoted text: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26/adopted — retrieved 2026-11-23T11:58:46Z, sha256 3afbbd1054e3 (harness-fetched page content).

Version banner appearing on that page, quoted verbatim:

  "Status: This is the original version as it was originally adopted in the EU.
   This legislation may since have been updated - see the latest available
   (revised) version"

That banner is the basis for treating the quoted wording as the original adopted text, which is what the request specifies.

====================================================================
3. SUPPORTING ELEMENTS OF THE SAME ARTICLE (context only, not part of the deadline)
====================================================================
These are quoted from the same fetched page and are included so the reviewer can see the surrounding mechanics. None of them changes the deadline in section 1.

(a) Routing of the report — Article 26(1), second subparagraph:
  "The competent authorities shall, in accordance with Article 85 of Directive
   2014/65/EU, establish the necessary arrangements in order to ensure that the
   competent authority of the most relevant market in terms of liquidity for
   those financial instruments also receives that information."

(b) Who may submit, and where responsibility sits — Article 26(7):
  "The reports shall be made to the competent authority either by the investment
   firm itself, an ARM acting on its behalf or by the trading venue through whose
   system the transaction was completed, in accordance with paragraphs 1, 3 and 9."
  "Investment firms shall have responsibility for the completeness, accuracy and
   timely submission of the reports which are submitted to the competent authority."
  (with a derogation for failures attributable to an ARM or trading venue, and a
   duty on firms to "take reasonable steps to verify the completeness, accuracy and
   timeliness of the transaction reports which were submitted on their behalf").

(c) Correction of errors — Article 26(7), final subparagraph:
  "Where there are errors or omissions in the transaction reports, the ARM,
   investment firm or trading venue reporting the transaction shall correct the
   information and submit a corrected report to the competent authority."

(d) Delegation to technical standards — Article 26(9) opens: "ESMA shall develop
   draft regulatory technical standards to specify:" (the enumerated list is not
   reproduced here; see review point R3).

(e) Scope of the obligation — Article 26(2) applies the paragraph 1 obligation to
   "(a) financial instruments which are admitted to trading or traded on a trading
   venue or for which a request for admission to trading has been made; (b) financial
   instruments where the underlying is a financial instrument traded on a trading
   venue; and" (list continues beyond the fetched snippet).

====================================================================
4. PERIOD, CURRENCY AND BASIS STATEMENT (per house constraint)
====================================================================
- Period: one working day, measured from the day of execution. The deadline is expressed as a point in time — the close of the working day following execution — not as a number of hours.
- Currency: not applicable. The provision contains no monetary amount, so no currency and no currency conversion arise.
- Basis of the number: the words "no later than the close of the following working day" are quoted directly from Article 26(1); there is no computation, estimation or arithmetic in this deliverable. Arithmetic shown: none required (0 additions, 0 multiplications, 0 divisions). The only quantity stated is the integer 1, implicit in "the following working day", and it is not aggregated or compared against any threshold anywhere in this note.
- Basis of the text: original adopted text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, English language version, as reproduced on the legislation.gov.uk 'adopted' page cited above.
- Date of adoption stated in the request: 15 May 2014. Date of OJ publication referenced in the request's own framing: 12 June 2014. This note cites the adopted-text wording; it does not re-verify the OJ publication date.

====================================================================
5. SCOPE AND EXCLUSIONS
====================================================================
- In scope: the primary deadline in the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014.
- Out of scope and excluded from the answer: any later amending regulation, consolidated version, corrigendum, or level-2/level-3 material. The request expressly confines the answer to the original text, and section 1 reflects only that text.
- Out of scope: national transposition or designation of the competent authority. The request supplies the concept ('the competent authority') and this note does not analyse which national body that is.

====================================================================
6. REVIEW POINTS FOR THE QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL (flagged, not resolved)
====================================================================
R1. Provenance. The quoted wording above is taken from the legislation.gov.uk reproduction of the 'adopted' EU text, not from the Official Journal itself. Before this note is relied on externally, the reviewer should confirm the wording character-for-character against the OJ publication of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 (cross-check links supplied in the research trail: EUR-Lex CELEX 32014R0600 and the ELI address https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/600/oj/eng). This is a verification step, not an open question about the answer.
R2. Later versions. A consolidated version dated 2024-12-04 was among the sources consulted for version-control purposes only. Its content is deliberately not described or relied on here, because the request confines the answer to the original text. If the reviewer needs the position as currently in force, that is a separate question and a separate note.
R3. Level-2 technical standards. Article 26(9) requires ESMA to develop draft regulatory technical standards. Whether those standards add technical timing, format or transmission requirements around the Article 26(1) deadline is not addressed here. The answer in section 1 is the primary legislative deadline only; it is not a statement that no further technical timing requirements exist.
R4. 'Working day'. The provision uses 'working day' without arithmetic conversion in this note. If a reviewer needs the operative definition for a specific jurisdiction or calendar, that definition should be confirmed from the regulation's definitions article and any applicable national calendar; this note does not resolve it.
R5. Anti-avoidance reading. Nothing in this note should be read as an opinion on whether a particular firm's reporting arrangements satisfy 'as quickly as possible' in any given case. That is a supervisory question for the reviewer.

====================================================================
7. DISCLAIMER
====================================================================
This is a draft working note prepared by a compliance analyst for review by a qualified finance, accounting or legal professional. It is not financial, tax, investment or legal advice, and it must not be relied on or circulated outside the review process until the review points in section 6 have been cleared.

Tax on unearned income of certain children.
Form 8615 must be filed for any child who meets all of the following conditions.
The child has more than $2,700 of unearned income.
The child is required to file a tax return.
The child either:
Was under age 18 at the end of 2025,
Was age 18 at the end of 2025 and didn’t have earned income that was more than half of the child's support, or
Was a full-time student at least age 19 and under age 24 at the end of 2025 and didn’t have earned income that was more than half of the child's support.
At least one of the child's parents was alive at the end of 2025.
The child doesn’t file a joint return for 2025.

verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED TAX PROFESSIONAL — NOT TAX, LEGAL OR INVESTMENT ADVICE.

PERIOD: tax year 2025 (returns filed in 2026). CURRENCY: USD. BASIS: US federal individual income tax, statutory basis IRC section 1411, as described in IRS Publication 550 (2025). SOURCE EDITION: Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses, 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns' — listed as current on https://www.irs.gov/publications and read at https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550 (HTML) and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf (PDF), fetched 2026-11-23.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER
=====================================================================
1.1 RATE — 3.8% (decimal 0.038).
    Equivalent expressions: 0.038 = 3.8% = $38 of tax per $1,000 of base (0.038 x 1,000 = 38.00).

1.2 AMOUNT TO WHICH THE RATE IS APPLIED (the base) — the LESSER of two candidate amounts:
      (a) net investment income; or
      (b) the amount by which modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) exceeds the threshold amount for the filer's filing status.
    If (b) is zero or negative, the base is zero and no NIIT is due.

    Base = MIN( NII , MAX(0, MAGI - T) )
      where NII = net investment income (section 1411 definition)
            MAGI = modified adjusted gross income
            T = threshold amount by filing status (table 2.2 below)
      NIIT = 0.038 x Base

1.3 The rate is therefore NOT applied to all net investment income in every case. It is applied to the full net investment income only where MAGI exceeds the threshold by at least the amount of net investment income; otherwise the base is the (smaller) MAGI excess.

=====================================================================
2. SOURCE TEXT (both figures come from this single passage)
=====================================================================
2.1 Quoted verbatim from Pub. 550 (2025), General Information, item 'Net investment income tax (NIIT).':

    'The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.'

    The HTML page (irs.gov/publications/p550) and the PDF (irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf) render this paragraph word-for-word identically; the PDF text reads 'The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.' No discrepancy between renderings.

2.2 Threshold table, as printed immediately after that paragraph in Pub. 550 (2025):

    Filing Status                                        Threshold Amount (USD)
    Married Filing Jointly or Qualifying Surviving Spouse      250,000
    Married Filing Separately                                  125,000
    Single or Head of Household                                200,000

2.3 Pub. 550 directs the reader onward for detail: 'See Code section 1411, Form 8960 and the Instructions for Form 8960 for more information.' That cross-reference is part of the sourced answer; the computation detail (what is included in net investment income, how MAGI is adjusted) is not set out in the quoted passage and must be taken from Form 8960 and its instructions.

=====================================================================
3. ARITHMETIC OF THE BASE — CANDIDATE AMOUNTS AND THE LESSER-OF SELECTION
=====================================================================
Step 1  Compute NII (candidate a). Source of components: section 1411 / Form 8960 — outside the Pub. 550 passage.
Step 2  Compute MAGI. Source: section 1411 / Form 8960 — outside the Pub. 550 passage.
Step 3  Look up T from table 2.2 by filing status.
Step 4  MAGI excess (candidate b) = MAGI - T. If the result is negative, use 0 (the tax cannot be applied to a negative amount; Pub. 550's phrase is 'the amount ... that is over a threshold', which is nil when MAGI is at or below the threshold).
Step 5  Base = the smaller of Step 1 and Step 4.
Step 6  NIIT = 0.038 x Base.

Control check applied to every illustration below: 0 <= NIIT <= 0.038 x NII and 0 <= NIIT <= 0.038 x MAGI excess. Any figure breaching either bound signals an error in the lesser-of selection.

=====================================================================
4. WORKED ILLUSTRATIONS (hypothetical figures, USD, tax year 2025)
=====================================================================
These are arithmetic demonstrations only; they are not a computation for any actual taxpayer.

4.1 Single filer; NII 60,000.00; MAGI 230,000.00
    T (Single) = 200,000.00                       [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  60,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 230,000.00 - 200,000.00 = 30,000.00
    Base = MIN(60,000.00, 30,000.00) =  30,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 30,000.00         =   1,140.00
    Checks: 1,140.00 <= 0.038 x 60,000.00 = 2,280.00  OK
            1,140.00 <= 0.038 x 30,000.00 = 1,140.00  OK (binding constraint is (b))

4.2 Married filing jointly; NII 40,000.00; MAGI 600,000.00
    T (MFJ) = 250,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  40,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 600,000.00 - 250,000.00 = 350,000.00
    Base = MIN(40,000.00, 350,000.00) =  40,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 40,000.00         =   1,520.00
    Checks: 1,520.00 <= 0.038 x 40,000.00 = 1,520.00  OK (binding constraint is (a))
            1,520.00 <= 0.038 x 350,000.00 = 13,300.00 OK
    Point: here the rate applies to ALL of NII — the common case, but only because (b) exceeds (a).

4.3 Married filing jointly; NII 90,000.00; MAGI 240,000.00
    T (MFJ) = 250,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 240,000.00 - 250,000.00 = (10,000.00) -> floored at 0.00
    Base = MIN(90,000.00, 0.00) = 0.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 0.00 = 0.00
    Point: MAGI below the threshold means no NIIT regardless of the size of NII.

4.4 Married filing separately; NII 10,000.00; MAGI 140,000.00
    T (MFS) = 125,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  10,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 140,000.00 - 125,000.00 = 15,000.00
    Base = MIN(10,000.00, 15,000.00) =  10,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 10,000.00         =     380.00
    Checks: 380.00 <= 0.038 x 10,000.00 = 380.00 OK; 380.00 <= 0.038 x 15,000.00 = 570.00 OK

4.5 Summary tie-out table (all figures USD, tax year 2025)
    Case | Status | NII        | MAGI        | T        | (b)=MAGI-T | Base       | NIIT
    4.1  | Single |  60,000.00 |  230,000.00 | 200,000  |  30,000.00 |  30,000.00 | 1,140.00
    4.2  | MFJ    |  40,000.00 |  600,000.00 | 250,000  | 350,000.00 |  40,000.00 | 1,520.00
    4.3  | MFJ    |  90,000.00 |  240,000.00 | 250,000  |       0.00 |       0.00 |     0.00
    4.4  | MFS    |  10,000.00 |  140,000.00 | 125,000  |  15,000.00 |  10,000.00 |   380.00
    Total NIIT across the four illustrative cases = 1,140.00 + 1,520.00 + 0.00 + 380.00 = 3,040.00. Each line ties to its own Base x 0.038; the total ties to the sum of the four bases (30,000 + 40,000 + 0 + 10,000 = 80,000) x 0.038 = 3,040.00. OK.

=====================================================================
5. DISAMBIGUATION — 'NET INVESTMENT INCOME' HAS TWO MEANINGS IN PUB. 550
=====================================================================
5.1 NIIT base (section 1411). The quoted General Information paragraph, sourced to Code section 1411 and Form 8960. This is the meaning used in this answer.
5.2 Investment interest expense limitation (chapter 3 of Pub. 550). Pub. 550 states: 'Determine the amount of your net investment income by subtracting your investment expenses (other than interest expense) from your investment income' and 'Generally, your deduction for investment interest expense is limited to your net investment income.' This is a different measure used for the section 163(d) deduction limit and is NOT the NIIT base. A preparer must not substitute one for the other. Flagged because both appear in the same publication under the same label.

=====================================================================
6. SCOPE LIMITS AND ITEMS THE QUOTED PASSAGE DOES NOT RESOLVE
=====================================================================
Each item below is named as a limit, not answered with an unsourced figure.
6.1 Estates and trusts. Pub. 550's quoted table covers individual filing statuses only. Section 1411 applies a separate threshold to estates and trusts, set by reference to the top bracket under section 1(e). The 2025 dollar amount is NOT in the quoted passage and is not stated here; obtain it from the 2025 Instructions for Form 8960 or the applicable annual inflation Revenue Procedure before use.
6.2 Nonresident aliens. Section 1411 does not apply to nonresident aliens; this exclusion is not in the quoted passage. Confirm against Form 8960 instructions before relying on it.
6.3 Thresholds and inflation. The three amounts in table 2.2 are the amounts Pub. 550 (2025) prints for 2025. Whether they are indexed is a statutory question (section 1411(b)) outside the quoted passage; do not assume indexation either way without checking the statute or the current Form 8960 instructions.
6.4 MAGI adjustments and the composition of NII (e.g. excluded categories, gains on property held for investment, self-employment and S-corp/partnership passive items) are governed by section 1411 and Form 8960, not by the quoted paragraph. Not reproduced here.
6.5 Jurisdiction. US federal only. State-level analogues (e.g. state net investment income taxes) are out of scope.
6.6 Edition control. The figures above are from the 2025 edition of Pub. 550 (identified on irs.gov/publications as 'Publication 550 (2025)' and internally as 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns'). If a later revision of Pub. 550 or a post-publication development changes the paragraph, the 'What's New' page at IRS.gov/Pub550 governs; re-verify before filing. The rate and thresholds are statutory and have been stable, but the edition actually used must be evidenced in the workpapers.

=====================================================================
7. SIGN-OFF BLOCK
=====================================================================
Prepared by: Finance Office (draft). Period: tax year 2025. Currency: USD. Basis: US federal individual income tax; IRC section 1411 as described in IRS Publication 550 (2025), General Information, 'Net investment income tax (NIIT)', cross-referenced to Form 8960 and its instructions. Rate sourced to the same paragraph; thresholds sourced to the table printed with that paragraph. Every figure above carries its source, period, currency and basis, and every computed NIIT has been checked against the lesser-of bounds. Status: DRAFT — requires review and sign-off by a qualified tax professional; not tax advice.

Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast) (Text with EEA relevance) (c. 138) xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"							
						



TITLE IU.K.GENERAL RULES ON THE TAKING-UP AND PURSUIT OF DIRECT INSURANCE AND REINSURANCE ACTIVITIES

CHAPTER VIU.K.Rules relating to the valuation of assets and liabilities, technical provisions, own funds, Solvency Capital Requirement, Minimum Capital Requirement and investment rules

Section 4U.K.Solvency capital requirement

Subsection 1U.K.General provisions for the solvency capital requirement using the standard formula or an internal model

Article 101U.K.Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement

1.The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated in accordance with paragraphs 2 to 5.

2.The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated on the presumption that the undertaking will pursue its business as a going concern.

3.The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.

It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period.

4.The Solvency Capital Requirement shall cover at least the following risks:

(a)non-life underwriting risk;

(b)life underwriting risk;

(c)health underwriting risk;

(d)market risk;

(e)credit risk;

(f)operational risk.

Operational risk as referred to in point (f) of the first subparagraph shall include legal risks, and exclude risks arising from strategic decisions, as well as reputation risks.

5.When calculating the Solvency Capital Requirement, insurance and reinsurance undertakings shall take account of the effect of risk-mitigation techniques, provided that credit risk and other risks arising from the use of such techniques are properly reflected in the Solvency Capital Requirement.

verdict.summary:
MEMO — SOLVENCY CAPITAL REQUIREMENT CALIBRATION IN DIRECTIVE 2009/138/EC: STATED PROBABILITY, STATED HORIZON, AND EQUIVALENT RUIN FREQUENCY

Draft for review by a qualified finance/accounting or actuarial professional. Not legal, tax or investment advice. All figures below carry their source provision and their arithmetic.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER IN BRIEF
=====================================================================

| Item | Answer | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Probability stated for the SCR | Confidence level of 99,5 % (Value-at-Risk) | STATED in the Directive | Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph |
| Implied probability of breaching the SCR / ruin per year | 0,5 % p.a. (= 100 % - 99,5 %) | DERIVED from the stated confidence level | Arithmetic on Art. 101(3) |
| Time horizon stated for the SCR | One-year period (existing business plus new business expected to be written over the following 12 months) | STATED in the Directive | Art. 101(3), 1st and 2nd subparagraphs |
| Equivalent ruin frequency | Once in 200 years — a mean return period of 200 years, i.e. a 1-in-200-year event | DERIVED: 1 / (1 - 0,995) = 1 / 0,005 = 200 | Arithmetic on Art. 101(3) |

Key caveat (read before relying on the last row): the Directive's own wording expresses the calibration as a Value-at-Risk at a 99,5 % confidence level over a one-year period. The Directive does not itself use a 'once in N years' formulation. The 1-in-200-years figure is the exact arithmetic equivalent of the Directive's stated confidence level and horizon, and is the formulation used in the Level 2 material and supervisory practice; it is presented here as a derived equivalence, not as a verbatim quotation from the Directive.

=====================================================================
2. SOURCE AND BASIS
=====================================================================

- Instrument: Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast), OJ L 335, 17.12.2009, p. 1-155; CELEX 32009L0138.
- Language version read: English.
- Text version relied on: 'Original (As adopted by EU)' — the version as it stood when first adopted, with no changes applied — as republished on legislation.gov.uk (eurdr/2009/138), plus the EUR-Lex CELEX landing pages for identification of the instrument.
- Provision in scope: Title I, Chapter VI (Rules relating to the valuation of assets and liabilities, technical provisions, own funds, Solvency Capital Requirement, Minimum Capital Requirement and investment rules), Section 4 (Solvency capital requirement), Subsection 1 (General provisions for the solvency capital requirement using the standard formula or an internal model), Article 101 (Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement), paragraph 3.
- Basis of the numbers: a regulatory calibration expressed as a probability (confidence level) over a defined period. No monetary amounts are involved; no currency applies. All percentages are as printed in the Directive, which uses a comma decimal separator ('99,5 %').

=====================================================================
3. THE OPERATIVE PROVISION — VERBATIM
=====================================================================

Article 101(3) of Directive 2009/138/EC (original, as adopted), verbatim:

  '3. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.

  It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period.'

Context (Article 101(1) and (2), same source, verbatim):

  '1. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated in accordance with paragraphs 2 to 5.'

  '2. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated on the presumption that the undertaking will pursue its business as a going concern.'

Article 101(4) and (5) (verbatim, for completeness) list the risks to be covered — non-life, life and health underwriting risk, market risk, credit risk, operational risk — and require account to be taken of risk-mitigation techniques. Neither paragraph restates or alters the probability or the horizon; the calibration figure appears once, in Article 101(3).

=====================================================================
4. STATED FIGURES, WITH ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================

4.1 Probability (stated)
  Stated value: confidence level 99,5 % (Value-at-Risk of basic own funds).
  Source: Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph ('... subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % ...').
  Note on what this is a probability of: it is the confidence level of a Value-at-Risk on basic own funds, i.e. the SCR is set at the level of loss in basic own funds that is exceeded with 0,5 % probability over the horizon. It is not expressed in the Directive as a 'probability of ruin' or 'probability of default' as such; the 0,5 % tail probability is the equivalent reading.

4.2 Time horizon (stated)
  Stated value: one year.
  Source: Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph ('... over a one-year period').
  Corroborating horizon language in the same paragraph: the SCR 'shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months' — i.e. a 12-month forward window, consistent with the one-year period.

4.3 Implied annual ruin probability (derived)
  Arithmetic: 100,0 % - 99,5 % = 0,5 % per annum.
  Basis: complement of the stated confidence level. This is an arithmetic identity, not an additional statement in the Directive.

4.4 Equivalent ruin frequency (derived)
  Arithmetic: 1 / 0,5 % = 1 / 0,005 = 200 years.
  Equivalently, as a frequency: 0,005 per annum = once in 200 years = a '1-in-200-year event'.
  Consistency check: 0,5 % x 200 = 100 % (the full probability mass is exhausted over 200 annual periods); 1 - 0,995 = 0,005 (the complement used is exactly the Directive's own figure).
  Interpretation: 200 years is the mean return period of the SCR-breach event under a stationary annual loss distribution — the mean of the geometric distribution with p = 0,005, which is 1/p = 200. It is not a claim that a breach will occur exactly every 200 years.

=====================================================================
5. WHAT THE DIRECTIVE DOES NOT SAY (PROVENANCE CAVEAT)
=====================================================================

- The Directive's original text does not contain the phrase 'once in 200 years', '1-in-200', '200-year event', or any other explicit return-period formulation. It states a 99,5 % confidence level over a one-year period and nothing more on calibration.
- The '1-in-200-years' formulation is the conventional regulatory and market gloss on that calibration and appears in Level 2/Level 3 material (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 and EIOPA guidance). Those texts were not retrieved and verified in this session; treat the attribution of the phrasing to those instruments as unverified background, flagged for the reviewer. The figure itself (200 years) does not depend on that attribution — it follows arithmetically from Article 101(3) alone.
- Recitals of the Directive were not retrieved and verified in this session. No reliance is placed on any recital; the operative calibration is in Article 101(3).
- Later amendments: the wording quoted above is from the as-adopted (original) version. Amendments made after adoption (e.g. by Omnibus II, Directive 2014/51/EU, and the Solvency II review amendments) were not checked here; the figure in Article 101(3) is the one the question asks about, and the reviewer should confirm whether any consolidated version in use in their jurisdiction renumbers or re-words it.
- The UK 'EU Exit' version of the same Article 101 shown on legislation.gov.uk carries the identical calibration wording (99,5 %, one-year period); it is noted only because that is the retrieval route for the original text, and no substantive difference was observed in the paragraphs quoted.

=====================================================================
6. POINTS FOR THE REVIEWING PROFESSIONAL
=====================================================================

1. Precision of language: the Directive calibrates the SCR as a Value-at-Risk on basic own funds at 99,5 % over one year. It does not define 'ruin' or 'insolvency probability'. If a document you are reviewing asserts that 'the Directive requires a 0,5 % probability of ruin', the accurate statement is that the Directive requires a 99,5 % one-year VaR, whose equivalent tail probability is 0,5 % per annum (a 1-in-200-year event).
2. Horizon: the one-year period is the risk horizon. It is distinct from the run-off / going-concern assumptions in Article 101(2) and from the 12-month new-business window in Article 101(3).
3. No currency: no monetary amount is set by the calibration provision; the SCR amount is undertaking-specific. Any figure in a downstream model that carries a currency must come from that model, not from Article 101.
4. Use of the 200-year figure: it is exact given the stated confidence level (1 / 0,005 = 200). Rounding to 'about 200 years' or 'a 1-in-200-year event' is acceptable; quoting any other return period (e.g. 100 or 250 years) would not agree with the Directive's stated 99,5 %.

=====================================================================
7. SOURCE-VERIFICATION LOG
=====================================================================

- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/138/article/101/data.xht?view=snippet&wrap=true — verbatim Article 101(1)-(5) of Directive 2009/138/EC, including the '99,5 %' / 'one-year period' sentence; fetched 2026-11-23T12:04:50Z, sha256 ce93646eb35f.
- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/138/article/101 — same Article; page identifies the version as 'Original (As adopted by EU)'; fetched 2026-11-23T12:04:04Z, sha256 01828fe1d6cb.
- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/en/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32009L0138 and https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009L0138 — EUR-Lex records for the instrument (identification of Directive 2009/138/EC, CELEX 32009L0138); listed as sources but the calibration sentence was read from the legislation.gov.uk as-adopted text above.
- Not retrieved/verified in this session: the recitals of Directive 2009/138/EC; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35; EIOPA guidance; any consolidated version incorporating post-2009 amendments.

=====================================================================
8. ONE-LINE ANSWER
=====================================================================

Article 101(3) of Directive 2009/138/EC (original text, as adopted) sets the SCR as the Value-at-Risk of basic own funds at a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period; the equivalent ruin frequency is 1 / (1 - 0,995) = 1 / 0,005 = 200 years, i.e. a 1-in-200-year event (0,5 % per annum).

quotes.whole:
§ 329.21 High-quality liquid asset amount.
(a) Calculation of the HQLA amount.  As of the calculation date, a FDIC-supervised institution's HQLA amount equals:
(1) The level 1 liquid asset amount; plus
(2) The level 2A liquid asset amount; plus
(3) The level 2B liquid asset amount; minus
(4) The greater of:
(i) The unadjusted excess HQLA amount; and
(ii) The adjusted excess HQLA amount.
(b) Calculation of liquid asset amounts —
(1) Level 1 liquid asset amount.  The level 1 liquid asset amount equals the fair value of all level 1 liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA, less the amount of the reserve balance requirement under section 204.5 of Regulation D (12 CFR 204.5).
(2) Level 2A liquid asset amount.  The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.
(3) Level 2B liquid asset amount.  The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA.

verdict.summary:
12 CFR PART 329 HQLA HAIRCUT CALCULATION — LEVEL 2A AND LEVEL 2B LIQUID ASSET AMOUNTS (DRAFT FOR REVIEW)

====================================================================
1. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS
====================================================================
Entity type: FDIC-supervised institution (12 CFR Part 329 applies).
As-of date / period: the institution's 'calculation date' as that term is used in 329.21; no specific calendar date was supplied, so no dated period is asserted. Every figure below is "as of the calculation date."
Currency: US dollars (USD). All amounts in millions of USD unless stated.
Basis of the input figures: fair value of assets held as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA, as given in the request. The request states all assets are eligible HQLA, so no eligibility or operational screening under 329.20/329.22 is performed here.
Basis of the output figures: the regulatory liquid asset amounts defined in 329.21(b)(2) and 329.21(b)(3) — i.e., a fixed percentage of fair value — NOT fair value itself, and NOT the cap-constrained HQLA amount of 329.21(a).
Constraint applied (ask 1): other caps and adjustments are IGNORED. Specifically excluded: the level 2 cap excess amount (329.21(d), the 0.6667 x level 1 factor), the level 2B cap excess amount (329.21(e), the 0.1765 x (level 1 + level 2A) factor), the unadjusted and adjusted excess HQLA amounts (329.21(c), (g)), the adjusted liquid asset amounts arising from unwinding transactions maturing within 30 calendar days (329.21(f)), and the Regulation D reserve balance requirement deduction (329.21(b)(1), which applies to level 1 only).
Status: draft prepared for review by a qualified finance/accounting professional. Not regulatory, tax or investment advice.

2. OPERATIVE REGULATORY TEXT (SOURCE OF THE PERCENTAGES)
====================================================================
Source: 12 CFR 329.21(b), as reproduced on the cited page — eCFR, 12 CFR Part 329, section 329.21 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-III/subchapter-B/part-329/section-329.21, fetched 2026-11-23T12:08:43Z, sha256 ca896132ac72). The same two sentences appear verbatim in the GovInfo XML of CFR 2026 title 12 vol 5, part 329 (sha256 ce49f4018311) and the GovInfo PDF of part 329 subpart C (sha256 f6952464872a), so the text is corroborated across three renderings of the cited page.

329.21(b)(2): "Level 2A liquid asset amount. The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

329.21(b)(3): "Level 2B liquid asset amount. The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

Implied haircuts: level 2A 15% (100% - 85%); level 2B 50% (100% - 50%). Only these two percentages enter the requested figures.

====================================================================
3. INPUTS (EACH LABELLED AS GIVEN OR ASSUMED)
====================================================================
I-1  Fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets ............ $80,000,000   [GIVEN in request]
I-2  Fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets ............ $30,000,000   [GIVEN in request]
I-3  Level 2A percentage per 329.21(b)(2) ..................... 85% = 0.85   [SOURCE: quoted text, section 2]
I-4  Level 2B percentage per 329.21(b)(3) ..................... 50% = 0.50   [SOURCE: quoted text, section 2]
A-1  [ASSUMPTION] The stated amounts are fair value on the regulatory basis used in 329.21 (i.e., no further valuation adjustment is required before applying the percentages). If a reviewer determines otherwise, the percentages apply to the corrected fair value, not to these inputs.
A-2  [ASSUMPTION] All stated assets are eligible HQLA as of the calculation date (given in the request), so 329.22 operational and generally-applicable criteria are satisfied and no exclusion is made.
A-3  [ASSUMPTION] No level 1 liquid assets are in scope of this calculation (none were provided); the level 1 liquid asset amount is therefore not computed and is not needed because the caps that would use it are excluded per ask 1.
A-4  [ASSUMPTION] No assets are held in a foreign jurisdiction requiring the currency/jurisdiction conditions in 329.20(b)(2)(ii) or 329.20(b)(3)(2)(ii) to be tested; classification as level 2A/level 2B is taken as given.

====================================================================
4. CALCULATION — LEVEL 2A LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT
====================================================================
Formula (329.21(b)(2)): Level 2A liquid asset amount = 0.85 x fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets
Arithmetic: 0.85 x $80,000,000 = $68,000,000
  80,000,000 x 0.85 = 80,000,000 x (0.80 + 0.05) = 64,000,000 + 4,000,000 = 68,000,000
Haircut retained against the institution: $80,000,000 - $68,000,000 = $12,000,000 (15%).
RESULT: Level 2A liquid asset amount = $68,000,000.

====================================================================
5. CALCULATION — LEVEL 2B LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT
====================================================================
Formula (329.21(b)(3)): Level 2B liquid asset amount = 0.50 x fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets
Arithmetic: 0.50 x $30,000,000 = $15,000,000
  30,000,000 x 0.50 = 15,000,000
Haircut retained against the institution: $30,000,000 - $15,000,000 = $15,000,000 (50%).
RESULT: Level 2B liquid asset amount = $15,000,000.

====================================================================
6. CALCULATION — SUM (ASK 3)
====================================================================
Level 2A liquid asset amount ........ $68,000,000
Level 2B liquid asset amount ........ $15,000,000
Sum (level 2A + level 2B) ........... $83,000,000
Check: 68,000,000 + 15,000,000 = 83,000,000. In millions: 68 + 15 = 83.
RESULT: Sum = $83,000,000.

====================================================================
7. SUMMARY TABLE (USD, AS OF THE CALCULATION DATE)
====================================================================
Line | Item                                   | Fair value   | Percentage (source)      | Liquid asset amount | Arithmetic
-----+----------------------------------------+--------------+--------------------------+---------------------+----------------------------
  1  | Level 2A liquid assets (eligible HQLA) | 80,000,000   | 85% — 329.21(b)(2)       | 68,000,000          | 0.85 x 80,000,000
  2  | Level 2B liquid assets (eligible HQLA) | 30,000,000   | 50% — 329.21(b)(3)       | 15,000,000          | 0.50 x 30,000,000
  3  | Sum of lines 1 + 2                     | 110,000,000  | n/a (not a haircut line) | 83,000,000          | 68,000,000 + 15,000,000

Total fair value of the in-scope level 2 assets is $110,000,000; total haircut retained is $27,000,000 (12,000,000 + 15,000,000), which equals 110,000,000 - 83,000,000 — consistent.

====================================================================
8. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED (ASK 1 CONSTRAINT)
====================================================================
The following provisions of the cited page are reproduced in the source but are switched OFF for this calculation, exactly as instructed. They are listed so a reviewer can see they were considered and excluded, not overlooked:
(a) 329.21(a)(4) / 329.21(c)-(e) — unadjusted excess HQLA amount, comprising the level 2 cap excess amount (greater of [level 2A + level 2B - 0.6667 x level 1] and 0) and the level 2B cap excess amount (greater of [level 2B - level 2 cap excess - 0.1765 x (level 1 + level 2A)] and 0). The 0.6667 factor is the 40%-of-level-1 level 2 cap; the 0.1765 factor is the 15%-of-level-1 level 2B cap.
(b) 329.21(f)-(i) — adjusted liquid asset amounts and the adjusted excess HQLA amount arising from unwinding secured funding/lending, asset exchanges and collateralized derivatives transactions maturing within 30 calendar days.
(c) 329.21(b)(1) — the Regulation D reserve balance requirement deduction (level 1 only; no level 1 assets in scope).
(d) Any other eligibility, operational, diversification or hedging-related reduction under 329.22.
MEMO NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER (does not change the answers above): because no level 1 liquid assets are in scope, if the caps were switched ON the level 2 cap excess amount would be 68,000,000 + 15,000,000 - 0.6667 x 0 = 83,000,000 and the level 2B cap excess amount would be 15,000,000 - 83,000,000 - 0.1765 x (0 + 68,000,000) = negative, i.e., floored at 0; the unadjusted excess HQLA amount would then be 83,000,000 and the 329.21(a) HQLA amount from these two lines would net to zero. The $68,000,000 / $15,000,000 / $83,000,000 figures in sections 4-7 are therefore PRE-CAP amounts, valid only under the 'ignoring other caps and adjustments' instruction, and must not be quoted as an HQLA amount under 329.21(a).

====================================================================

- Confirm USD and that the stated amounts are fair value on the 329.21 basis (assumption A-1).
- Confirm the calculation date if a dated workpaper is required.

findings.question:
1. A covered company subject to the single-counterparty credit limits in 12 CFR Part 252 has $40 billion of tier 1 capital and an $11 billion aggregate net credit exposure to one counterparty. As in force on 2026-11-21, what is its 25% exposure cap in dollars, by how much does the exposure exceed that cap, and is the separate 5% economic-interdependence and control-relationship assessment triggered?
2. The counterparty's status under 252.152 (e.g., whether it is the US or non-US parent company), since that determines whether the cap is 25% or 5%, or both
3. Whether the company qualifies for the $50 billion threshold treatment or is subject to the standard limits, since this changes which cap applies
4. Whether tier 1 capital of $40 billion is the correct regulatory measure on the relevant measurement date

no U.S. intermediate holding company ... may have an aggregate net credit exposure ... that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital
If a covered foreign entity has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered foreign entity must assess its relationship

§ 252.72 Credit exposure limits.




(a) General limit on aggregate net credit exposure.  No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company.





(b) Limit on aggregate net credit exposure of major covered companies to major counterparties.  No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company.

(d) Board determinations for aggregation of counterparties due to economic interdependence or control relationships.  The Board may determine, after notice to the covered company and opportunity for hearing, that one or more counterparties of a covered company are:
(1) Economically interdependent for purposes of this subpart, considering the factors in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, as well as any other indicia of economic interdependence that the Board determines in its discretion to be relevant; or

(i) Controls the power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of Counterparty B pursuant to a voting agreement;
(ii) Has significant influence on the appointment or dismissal of counterparty B's administrative, management, or governing body, or the fact that a majority of members of such body have been appointed solely as a result of the exercise of counterparty A's voting rights; or
(iii) Has the power to exercise a controlling influence over the management or policies of counterparty B.

verdict.summary:
# Single-Counterparty Credit Limit Test — 12 CFR Part 252, as in force 2026-11-21

DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE, ACCOUNTING OR REGULATORY-REPORTING PROFESSIONAL. Not financial, tax or investment advice, and not a legal opinion on the application of Regulation YY. All figures are USD unless stated.

---

## 1. Scope, period, currency and basis

| Dimension | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Entity | A 'covered company' subject to Subpart H of 12 CFR Part 252 (Single-Counterparty Credit Limits, §§ 252.70–252.79), i.e. subject to § 252.72(a). ASSUMPTION — the specific covered-company category is not given. The Subpart Q parallel regime for covered foreign entities is addressed in §7(d); it uses the same 25% ratio, so the arithmetic does not change. |
| Period / measurement date | A single measurement date, not specified in the request. ASSUMPTION: all figures are measured as of the same date (taken as 2026-11-21). Tier 1 capital and aggregate net credit exposure must be as of the same date; mixing dates would invalidate the ratio. |
| Currency | USD; no conversion applied. ASSUMPTION. |
| Basis — denominator | Tier 1 capital as defined in the Board's capital rule (12 CFR 217.20), i.e. regulatory tier 1 capital of the covered company, not GAAP equity. $40,000,000,000 is taken as given and is an ASSUMPTION; it has not been recomputed from a Call Report / FR Y-9C. |
| Basis — numerator | 'Aggregate net credit exposure' as computed under §§ 252.73–252.75 (gross credit exposure, less eligible collateral and netting, with the rule's prescribed treatment of eligible financial contracts, securities financing transactions and credit derivatives). $11,000,000,000 is taken as given and is an ASSUMPTION; it has not been recomputed and is assumed to include any aggregation already required. |
| Governing text date | Rule text as in force 2026-11-21, read from the eCFR 'current' pages fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:56Z–12:13:58Z. See §10 for the two-day residual risk. |

---

## 2. Authorities relied on (verbatim, with fetch provenance)

1. **§ 252.72(a) — general limit.** 'No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company.' (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-252.72, fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:56Z, sha256 cfa98394af04.)
2. **§ 252.72(b) — major covered company / major counterparty limit.** 'No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company.' (same source.)
3. **§ 252.76(a)(1) — 5% assessment trigger.** 'If a covered company has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered company must assess its relationship with the counterparty under paragraph (b)(2) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is economically interdependent with one or more other counterparties of the covered company and under paragraph (c)(1) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is connected by a control relationship with one or more other counterparties.' (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-252.76, fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:56Z, sha256 ca40090fa22e.)
4. **§ 252.76(a)(2) — consequence of the assessment.** If factors in (b)(2) or (c)(1) are met, or the Board so determines under (d), 'the covered company must aggregate its net credit exposure to the counterparties for all purposes under this subpart, including, but not limited to, § 252.72.' (same source.)
5. **§ 252.76(b)(2)/(c)(1) — the factors.** Inter alia: counterparty A guarantees ≥50% of the covered company's net credit exposure to counterparty B; ≥25% of one counterparty's production or output is sold to the other and cannot easily be replaced; the expected source of funds to repay both is the same with no independent source; two or more counterparties rely on the same source for the majority of their funding with no alternative provider. Control factors include power to vote ≥25% of a class of voting securities pursuant to a voting agreement, significant influence over appointment/dismissal of the governing body, or power to exercise a controlling influence over management or policies. (same source.)
6. **§ 252.76(b)(3) and (d).** The covered company may request a written Board determination that counterparties are not economically interdependent; the Board may also determine aggregation on its own initiative. (same source.)
7. **Subpart Q parallels.** § 252.172(b)(1): a U.S. intermediate holding company that is a covered foreign entity may not have aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty exceeding 25% of its tier 1 capital. § 252.176(a)(2)(i): 5% assessment trigger in identical terms. Subpart Q source note reads '83 FR 38501, Aug. 6, 2018, as amended at 84 FR 59121, Nov. 1, 2019'. (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-252/subpart-Q, fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:57Z, sha256 309a7a71aaca; .../subpart-H/section-252.176, sha256 7ba9a4280dbc.)

No amendment later than 2019 appears in the fetched text of either subpart.

---

## 3. Inputs, with source and status

| Ref | Input | Value (USD) | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Tier 1 capital of the covered company | 40,000,000,000 | Request | Given; ASSUMPTION that it is regulatory tier 1 capital (12 CFR 217.20) on the measurement date |
| B | Aggregate net credit exposure to the single counterparty | 11,000,000,000 | Request | Given; ASSUMPTION that it is computed under §§ 252.73–252.75 and already includes any aggregation required |
| C | General limit ratio | 25% | § 252.72(a) | Rule text |
| D | Assessment trigger ratio | 5% | § 252.76(a)(1) | Rule text |
| E | Major-company / major-counterparty ratio (not applied) | 15% | § 252.72(b) | Rule text; assumed inapplicable |

---

## 4. Ask 2 — the 25% exposure cap in dollars

Cap = C x A = 0.25 x 40,000,000,000 = **10,000,000,000 USD**

- Ratio applied: 25% (§ 252.72(a)).
- Basis: regulatory tier 1 capital of the covered company as of the measurement date.
- Period: measurement date (assumed 2026-11-21).
- Currency: USD.
- Arithmetic: 40,000,000,000 x 0.25 = 10,000,000,000.

**Answer to ask 2: $10,000,000,000 (ten billion dollars).**

---

## 5. Ask 3 — dollar amount by which the exposure exceeds the cap

Excess = B - Cap = 11,000,000,000 - 10,000,000,000 = **1,000,000,000 USD**

Supporting ratios (all on the same basis and date):

| Measure | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Exposure as % of tier 1 capital | 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 27.5% |
| Cap as % of tier 1 capital | 10,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 25.0% |
| Excess as % of tier 1 capital | 1,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 2.5% |
| Ratio check | 27.5% - 25.0% | 2.5% (agrees) |

**Answer to ask 3: $1,000,000,000 (one billion dollars) over the cap — a breach of § 252.72(a), which prohibits exposure 'that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital'. The position is not compliant; the exposure must be reduced, capital increased, or both (see §9).**

---

## 6. Ask 4 — is the 5% economic-interdependence / control-relationship assessment triggered?

Threshold = D x A = 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 = 2,000,000,000 USD

Test: is B > threshold? 11,000,000,000 > 2,000,000,000 → **YES, triggered.**

| Measure | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 5% threshold in dollars | 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| Exposure over the threshold | 11,000,000,000 - 2,000,000,000 | 9,000,000,000 |
| Exposure as a multiple of the threshold | 11,000,000,000 / 2,000,000,000 | 5.5x |
| Exposure as % of tier 1 capital (same figure as §5) | 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 27.5% (> 5%) |

**Answer to ask 4: Yes — the § 252.76(a)(1) assessment obligation is triggered.**

What 'triggered' does and does not mean:

- It is an **obligation to perform and document an assessment**, not a 5% exposure cap. Nothing in § 252.76 prohibits an exposure above 5% of tier 1 capital; the 5% figure is a threshold that switches on the analysis. (See §7(a).)
- The obligation is triggered by the size of the exposure alone. It is independent of the 25% breach in §5, and it is met here with 9,000,000,000 of headroom to spare.
- The **consequence is conditional**. Only if a factor in § 252.76(b)(2) (economic interdependence) or § 252.76(c)(1) (control relationship) is met — or the Board determines aggregation under § 252.76(d) — must the covered company aggregate its net credit exposure to the related counterparties 'for all purposes under this subpart, including … § 252.72'. Aggregation would raise the numerator and enlarge the breach quantified in §5; it cannot reduce it.
- The covered company may seek a written Board determination under § 252.76(b)(3) that identified counterparties are not economically interdependent.
- Because the 25% cap is already breached, the assessment cannot prudently be deferred: any aggregation finding increases an existing excess.

---

## 7. Framing points a reviewer should carry forward

**(a) The 5% figure is a trigger, not a limit.** The request describes a 'separate 5% … limit'. On the fetched text there is no 5% hard cap in Subpart H or Subpart Q. § 252.76(a)(1) / § 252.176(a)(2)(i) impose an assessment duty at 5% of tier 1 capital; the hard caps are 25% (§ 252.72(a) / § 252.172(b)) and, for major covered companies versus major counterparties, 15% (§ 252.72(b) / § 252.172(c)(2)). Any internal policy that treats 5% as a hard limit is an institution-specific appetite statement, not the rule.

**(b) Counterparty parent/affiliate status does not change the answer on the fetched text.** The fetched rule text contains no separate 5% (or other) cap keyed to whether the counterparty is the covered company's parent or a U.S. or non-U.S. affiliate. § 252.72 contains only (a) 25% and (b) 15%. If the reviewer's version of Part 252 (or an institution-specific interpretation) contains such a provision, re-run at that ratio; asks 2 and 3 are otherwise unaffected by counterparty status unless the 15% limb in (c) below applies.

**(c) The 15% limb is assumed inapplicable.** If the covered company were a 'major covered company' and the counterparty a 'major counterparty' (§ 252.71), the binding limit would be 0.15 x 40,000,000,000 = 6,000,000,000 and the excess 11,000,000,000 - 6,000,000,000 = 5,000,000,000. The request asks for the 25% cap, and the company is assumed not to be a major covered company facing a major counterparty. Confirm this before relying on the $10,000,000,000 figure as the binding constraint.

**(d) Subpart Q gives the same numbers.** For a U.S. intermediate holding company that is a covered foreign entity, § 252.172(b)(1) is also 25% of tier 1 capital → cap 10,000,000,000, excess 1,000,000,000; and § 252.176(a)(2)(i) is also a 5% assessment trigger → threshold 2,000,000,000, triggered. Note the different capital base: for a foreign banking organization under § 252.172(b)(2), the 25% is measured against the tier 1 capital of the foreign banking organization, not the combined U.S. operations.

---
